question.worked_solution:
First, we calculate the norm of the vector $x$ in terms of $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖x‖ & =\sqrt{{x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}+{x}_{4}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+(2k)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{1+9+4{k}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{10+4{k}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into the given equation  $‖x‖=5\sqrt{2},$ we obtain an equation that we can solve for $k:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\sqrt{10+4{k}^{2}} & =5\sqrt{2} \\ {(\sqrt{10+4{k}^{2}})}^{2} & ={(5\sqrt{2})}^{2} \\ 10+4{k}^{2} & =50 \\ 4{k}^{2} & =40 \\ {k}^{2} & =10 \\ k & =\pm \sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$
